Guides

What to know before the recipes.

The key points come first. The fuller explanation is on the same page, with links to the sources.

Foundations

What first foods are really for

In the second half of the first year, food is there for iron, energy, and learning to eat. It is not about hitting a protein percentage.

When to start

The right window opens after four months and runs to about six. Readiness is about skills, but there is still a minimum age.

Spoon, fingers, or both

Purées, finger foods, or a mix of both can all feed a baby well. The debate about which camp you’re in is louder than the evidence.

Choosing ingredients

Variety, bitter greens included, matters more than an organic label. Only a short list of foods is genuinely unsuitable.

Cooking and seasoning

Herbs, a mild spice, and a spoonful of oil do more for a baby’s food than salt or sugar ever will.

Tools, hygiene, and the freezer

A knife, a pan, and good fridge habits matter more than a drawer full of baby gadgets.

At the table

What to introduce, and when

There is no set calendar for which vegetable comes when. There is a good reason to bring in allergens early and keep them in the diet.

Introducing allergens

Delaying peanut, egg, and milk doesn’t prevent allergy. For most babies, the safer plan is to start them in a safe texture and keep them coming.

Portions, texture, and milk

Appetite is a better guide than counting spoonfuls. Milk stays the main drink until the first birthday.

A week, in outline

These are examples, not rules. Swap in whichever iron food and allergen you’re working on.

How mealtimes work

What goes on the table is up to you. Whether your child eats it, and how much, is up to them. Pressure is a poor teacher.

Gagging and choking

Gagging is loud and helpful. Choking is silent and an emergency. Learn the first-aid response before you need it.

Health and quick reference

Picky eating

Being wary of new food is a normal toddler stage. Your child’s growth, not today’s plate, tells you when to ask for help.

When your child is ill

Familiar food, enough fluids, and the usual milk feeds. A sick day is the wrong day to decide on an allergy or try a new food.

Teething

Cold food and something firm to chew are enough. Skip amber necklaces and benzocaine gels.

Vitamins and minerals

Vitamin D is a supplement decision from the first days. Iron is a food decision from six months. Everything else follows from the diet.
